headline: UK Doctors Develop Non-Invasive Womb Cancer Test
meta_description: UK doctors have created a simple test to rule out womb cancer in women experiencing postmenopausal bleeding, avoiding invasive procedures.
summary_short: A breakthrough test could spare thousands of women from uncomfortable, costly invasive procedures while detecting womb cancer early.
body:
UK doctors have developed a simple test that could help rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause. The approach has the potential to transform care for thousands of women each year.

Postmenopausal bleeding triggers urgent cancer referrals for hundreds of thousands of women worldwide annually. Many currently undergo invasive and uncomfortable diagnostic tests that can also strain healthcare budgets. This new development offers a less burdensome alternative.

By making early detection more accessible and less distressing, the test addresses a significant gap in women's health care. The innovation reflects a broader shift toward patient-centered medicine—one that maintains diagnostic accuracy while respecting patient comfort and reducing unnecessary strain on health systems.
quick_facts: UK doctors created a non-invasive womb cancer screening test
Targets women experiencing bleeding after menopause
Could spare thousands from uncomfortable invasive procedures annually
Hundreds of thousands diagnosed with womb cancer yearly worldwide
